gap.missing_evidence: No directly observed ED-eligible bed-offer events or availability intervals conditioned on destination specialty, time of day, weekday/season, or operational calendar are established by the inspected primary source. Hassanzadeh et al. report a ward-level DES using ED presentations, inpatient episodes, and ward-transfer movements at three Queensland hospitals; the source describes ward flow, bed capacities, and scenario interventions, but does not identify ED-facing offer occurrence, compatibility, expiry/withdrawal, or an offer denominator. Ward-movement timestamps and ward discharges are not equivalent to ED-eligible offers.
gap.owner: P1.1 coordinator and ED pathway/hospital-interface model owner
gap.impact: No empirical offer rate, availability process, specialty compatibility map, or temporal default can be populated from this source. Any labelled perturbation to an external offer stream remains a synthetic scenario assumption; it does not represent observed offers or establish the causal effects of ward discharge, elective-admission, or clustering interventions. R29's finite, specialty-compatible offer event is a separate proposed model boundary, not a finding or parameter from Hassanzadeh et al.
searches_performed: Inspected the bound primary article snapshot at .artifacts/sources/queensland-ward-des-pmc.html (SHA-256 ebc61c9fb85985ff9c0993320ab1a0f866d7ab490d4e30f93eaed4d4607aaeb5), Hassanzadeh et al., Medical Journal of Australia 2026, DOI 10.5694/mja2.70142, PMC12946774; local retrieval/access date 2026-10-01.

Read the article abstract and Methods sections 2.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.1.3 and 2.1.4 (HTML anchors mja270142-sec-0002, sec-0008, sec-0010 through sec-0018). Methods identify input records as ED presentations, inpatient episodes, and ward transfer movements at three principal referral hospitals; the activity period is 2021-03-01 to 2022-08-31, with 2021-09-01 to 2022-08-31 as the reported year. The model includes elective and ED admissions and verified-capacity wards.

Searched the pinned article text for offer, bed offer, availability, destination, specialty, transfer, discharge, timestamp, weekday, weekend, and season. It reports ward movement timing, ward capacities, and scenario definitions/outcomes; it does not specify ED-eligible offer event records, offer conditioning fields, offer denominator, expiry/withdrawal, or bed-management compatibility.

Kept supplied report R29 lineage separate: its lines 27-54 classify the ED-eligible compatible offer stream and proposed conditioning dimensions as boundary/model choices, while lines 200-212 identify persistence, destination granularity, and linked bed-management data as unresolved or priority acquisition. R29 is not primary evidence of an observed offer process.
gap.next_action: Obtain an approved linked ED-admitted-patient/bed-management event dataset or another primary source that records when an inpatient placement opportunity became eligible to be offered to an ED patient, destination specialty/unit compatibility, occurrence and expiry/withdrawal times, temporal/calendar fields, site/population/period, denominator, and competing non-ED demand. Bind that source separately and request independent readback before fitting or using any empirical input; preserve offer-stream changes as explicitly synthetic scenarios until then.
